newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BLUES BLANK BLACKHAWKS TO GRAB A PLAYOFF SPOT.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BLUES BLANK BLACKHAWKS TO GRAB A PLAYOFF SPOT.

text.p: Grant Fuhr recorded his third shutout of the season and Brett Hull scored the game's only goal as the St. Louis Blues clinched a playoff spot by blanking the Chicago Blackhawks 1-0 on Wednesday.
Fuhr turned aside 23 shots for the Blues/
Jeff Hackett made 22 saves for the Blackhawks, who played without injured captain Chris Chelios. The three-time Norris Trophy winner remains sidelined with a sore back.
Hull returned to the lineup after missing three games with a groin injury.

At Colorado, Bob Errey scored his first two goals in nearly two months, highlighting a three-goal third period that carried the lowly San Jose Sharks to their second win over the Colorado Avalanche in less than a week 4-1.
Viktor Kozlov also scored in the final period for the Sharks, who joined the Calgary Flames as the only teams to beat the defending Stanley Cup champions three times this season.
Mike Keane had the lone goal for the Avalanche.
In Dallas, Greg Adams, Benoit Hogue and Bob Bassen scored second-period goals and the red-hot Dallas Stars ran their home unbeaten streak to 11 games with a 3-2 victory over Toronto Maple Leafs.
Arturs Irbe had to make just 16 saves shots for Dallas, which is 10-1-4 in their last 15 games.
The Stars outshot Toronto, 43-18, and held the Leafs without a shot on goal for the first nine minutes of the third period.
In Edmonton, Tomas Sandstrom's shorthanded goal at 8:52 of the third period lifted the Detroit Red Wings into a 3-3 tie with the Edmonton Oilers.
Mike Vernon made 29 saves for the Red Wings.
Boris Mironov had a goal and an assist for the Oilers.

At Florida, Dave Lowry scored twice in a four-goal third period as the Florida Panthers strengthened their chances for home-ice advantage in the opening round of the playoffs by rallying for a 4-2 victory over the New Jersey Devils.
Rob Niedermayer and Radek Dvorak also scored in the third period for the Panthers.
"This was a big morale boost," Niedermayer said. "Beating a team like New Jersey and someone like Martin Brodeur, everyone has to feel confident after a game like this."
Jay Pandolfo and Bobby Holik scored for the Devils.

At the Islanders, Shayne Corson's power-play goal with 4:33 left in the third period snapped a tie and Jocelyn Thibault made 28 saves as the Montreal Canadiens topped the New York Islanders 3-1 to solidify their hold on seventh place in the Eastern Conference.
New York's Steve Webb took a costly slashing penalty with five minutes remaining in regulation and Corson broke a 1-1 tie 27 seconds later with his seventh goal of the season.
Vladimir Malakhov and Martin Rucinsky added goals for the Canadiens, who have won five of their last seven games.

In Ottawa, Randy Cunneyworth's power-play goal with 7:11 remaining snapped a tie as the Ottawa Senators moved into a tie for the final Eastern Conference playoff spot with a 5-4 victory over the Hartford Whalers.
Ron Tugnutt stopped 21 shots for Ottawa, which is tied with Hartford at 73 points. Both teams have two games remaining.
The Whalers still hold the tie-breaker edge by virtue of more wins. The Senators and Hartford are three points behind Montreal.

In Vancouver, Lonny Bohonos had two goals and an assist during a five-goal first period and Martin Gelinas added a pair of tallies and two assists as the Vancouver Canucks held on for a 6-4 victory over the Phoenix Coyotes, keeping their slim playoff hopes alive.
Donald Brashear and Bret Hedican also scored in the first period for the Canucks.
In Anaheim, David Karpa scored his second goal of the season with 16:48 to play to break a third-period tie as the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim beat the Los Angeles Kings 4-1.
Guy Hebert stopped 31 shots. Teemu Selanne scored his 50th goal.
Glen Murray scored the goal for Los Angeles.
